human_tolerance.notes: Breeds in urban areas as well as woodland and open farmland, and is 'not shy about nesting close to human habitations'. Forages in numbers on mown lawns and wherever sprinklers are running, and is a common pest in North American fruit orchards. The domestic cat is its main adult predator.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Breeding season runs April to July with two to three broods; among the earliest North American birds to lay eggs, starting soon after the return to the summer range.

phases.name: nesting
phases.note: Nest 1.5-4.5 m above ground in a dense bush or a fork between branches; clutch of three to five eggs, incubated by the female alone, hatching after 14 days; young leave the nest a further two weeks later.

phases.name: absent
phases.note: Most robins leave the northern United States by the end of August and return north in February and March.

phases.name: flocking
phases.note: Assembles in large flocks at night on the winter range.

vocalizations.description: A complex, almost continuous carol made of discrete repeated units spliced into a string with brief pauses; varies regionally and with time of day. Usually sung from a high perch, among the first songbirds singing before dawn and the last after sunset.

A sharp, rapid 'tuck-tuck' or 't-he-teh' scolding call, given when a ground predator approaches and when a nest or another robin is directly threatened; robins also band together to drive predators away.
A soft 'chup' or low 'tut-tut' contact call exchanged between a pair and between flock members on the winter ground.

external.note: eBird code ambri via Wikipedia's infobox.

range.note: Breeds throughout most of North America from Alaska and Canada south to northern Florida and Mexico; most winter south of Canada. Rare vagrant to western Europe and a handful of other places; the vagrancy is not treated as an introduced range.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Runs and hops on the ground taking 'several short hops and then cock its head', and flies.

traits.perching.note: Perches in trees and on wires, and 'usually sings from a high perch in a tree'.

traits.senses.note: Wikipedia states the species uses 'auditory, visual, olfactory and possibly vibrotactile cues to find prey, but vision is the predominant mode', and that experiments show it finds earthworms underground by listening alone. Olfaction is set to Med and hearing to High on that basis; no open source quantifies either, and vision_colour is omitted rather than guessed.

traits.mass_kg.note: Wikipedia gives an average of about 77 g, with males 72-94 g and females 59-91 g.

traits.length_m.note: Midpoint of Wikipedia's 23-28 cm length for the eastern subspecies.

traits.lifespan_y.note: 'the average lifespan is about two years'; the longest known wild bird is 14 years, and only 25% of young survive their first year.

traits.diet.note: Wikipedia's 'around 40 percent small invertebrates (mainly insects) ... and 60 percent wild and cultivated fruits and berries' gives invertebrate 0.4 and fruit 0.6; the schema's diet has no separate berry key, so the fruit-and-berry share is recorded as fruit.

traits.social.note: Breeds in territorial pairs and defends the nest against other robins, so Solitary with a group size of 1-2; the large winter night flocks are recorded under seasonal.phases as a flocking phase instead, since the schema's field describes an individual's social unit.

traits.activity_pattern.note: 'The species is active mostly during the day and assembles in large flocks at night.'

traits.defense.note: Flies off and gives alarm calls; also mobbing, which the schema offers as a separate single value, so Flee is chosen as the primary response.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: 0.35. It nests close to houses without shyness and feeds in numbers on mowed suburban lawns, but still gives alarm calls and moves off when a person approaches closely, and the cat predation it suffers is largely on suburban lawns.

habitat.use.note: The ground share follows Wikipedia's 'robins forage primarily on the ground' and its lawn-foraging description; the arboreal share covers perching to sing, night roosting and nesting in trees.

habitat.resources.note: Food weights follow traits.diet. Nesting in a cup in a bush or branch fork gives nest_cup its weight; perch and shrub_thicket are shelter and are weighted by judgement, since no open source compares their use.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Breeding habitat is given as 'woodland and more open farmland and urban areas', it is 'not shy about nesting close to human habitations', it is 'a common pest of fruit orchards', and 'in urban areas, robins will gather in numbers soon after lawns are mowed or where sprinklers are in use'. impervious_max and flight_distance_m are authored judgement on that description and are not quantified in the source.

habitat.density_per_ha.note: Judgement: Wikipedia's statement that this is 'the most abundant landbird in North America (with 370 million individuals)' fixes the order of magnitude for a continent-wide species; typical 1.7 per hectare follows from a typical breed-bird territory of roughly 0.6 ha, and min and max are an authored tenfold band either side, following the same convention used for sciurus-carolinensis and vulpes-vulpes.

seasonal.strategy.note: 'The species is a migratory bird', wintering south of Canada; a minority overwinters in the northern United States and southern Canada.

seasonal.winter_fraction.note: Judgement, from 'while robins occasionally overwinter in the northern part of the United States and southern Canada, most migrate'.

seasonal.phases.note: Breeding April to July with two to three broods; nest height, clutch size, 14-day incubation and nest-leaving timings from the Breeding section; departure and return dates from Distribution and habitat; night flocking from the lead paragraph.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Juvenile duration is authored: eggs hatch at 14 days, young leave the nest 14 days later and reach sustained flight two weeks after that, giving about 42 days to flight and roughly 90 days to independent foraging. scale is authored judgement.

vocalizations.note: The song description, its late-February to late-July period, the high song perch and the dawn-to-dusk singing window come from the Vocalization section; the alarm call's ground-predator and nest-threat contexts come from the same section. Months, cooldowns and the contact call are authored judgement, since no open source quantifies them. No open source gives frequency bands, so freq_hz is omitted.

look.note: Colours from the Description section: black to grey head with white eye arcs and supercilia, white throat with black streaks, white belly and undertail coverts, brown back, reddish-orange breast, mainly yellow bill with a dark tip, brown legs. Proportions and the breast and eye-arc parts are authored judgement to render the orange breast and the white eye arcs. The bill is mapped to the pale belly slot rather than yellow: the palette has five slots and the black head and orange breast take two of them, so the model reads pale-billed rather than yellow-billed. The back is held at a warm brown and only the head takes the near-black accent: a first pass put the wings and tail in the accent slot too and the bird rendered as a black blob from behind, which the previewer showed.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared perching-songbird program. flee_m raised from the European robin's 4 m to 8 m for a larger, bolder bird that forages on open lawns; food_tag, song, alarm, nest_m1 and nest_m2 follow the program's declared params and the nest height Wikipedia gives.
